axes.name: Perceptual foundations
axes.purpose: Formalize the structures that immediately organize perception of the interface.
focusAreas: global regions, composition, containment, and depth
grid, alignment, proportions, and spatial rhythm
density, whitespace, and salience hierarchy
typography, color, surfaces, borders, radii, and elevation
iconography, imagery, and visual language for data

axes.name: Task architecture
axes.purpose: Describe how the interface orients, prioritizes, and moves a user through a task.
focusAreas: orientation, navigation, and current location
information hierarchy and reading order
primary, secondary, and next-step actions
grouping, progressive disclosure, and cognitive load
context continuity across actions

axes.name: Interactions and state machine
axes.purpose: Define states, transitions, feedback, and modalities required for predictable interaction.
focusAreas: default, hover, focus, pressed, selected, and disabled states
loading, empty, error, success, warning, partial, and stale business states
feedback, confirmation, cancellation, and recovery
keyboard, touch, pointer, focus, and interactive targets
functional motion and user preferences

axes.name: Cross-cutting business and data patterns
axes.purpose: Turn visible business structures into reusable component and data contracts.
focusAreas: visible component anatomy and variants
tables, lists, cards, forms, and validation
search, filters, sorting, pagination, and batch actions
status, progress, KPIs, and data visualization
missing, partial, large, or heterogeneous content

axes.name: Adaptation and inclusion
axes.purpose: Preserve access to information and action across variations in context, content, and ability.
focusAreas: reflow, intrinsic responsiveness, zoom, and enlarged text
localization, expansion, cultural formats, and RTL
reading order, labels, focus, contrast, and alternatives
keyboard, touch, pointer, and assistive-technology equivalence
theme, contrast, text size, and reduced motion

axes.name: Perceived performance and resilience
axes.purpose: Keep the interface understandable and stable during delay, failure, and degradation.
focusAreas: priority and timing of loading states
visual stability and reserved space
partial, stale, offline, or unavailable data
error recovery, retry, and preservation of work
perceptual cost of lists, media, and visualizations

axes.name: Content, trust, and privacy
axes.purpose: Make labels, messages, and consequential decisions understandable and trustworthy.
focusAreas: clarity, tone, precision, and terminology
actionable errors and next steps
permissions, privacy, and collection rationale
data provenance, freshness, and limitations
destructive actions, consequences, and confirmation

axes.name: System and governance
axes.purpose: Convert observations and proposals into reusable, traceable, agent-verifiable rules.
focusAreas: semantic tokens and relationships between tokens
component contracts, variants, and anti-patterns
provenance, confidence, exceptions, and unknowns
framework-neutral design-to-code mapping
installation, overrides, audits, and non-regression

concepts.name: State and edge-case coverage
concepts.description: Inventory visible states and separately propose absent states required for a robust component.
inspect: displayed state and probable trigger
feedback, exit action, and context preservation
anatomy consistency across states
screenshotLimits: unshown states are never observed
transitions and timing are invisible in a static screenshot
stressTests: disabled, warning, success, and stale data

concepts.name: Iconographic coherence
concepts.description: Treat icons as one visual and semantic language rather than isolated decoration.
inspect: outline, filled, or mixed family
weight, caps, corners, bounding box, and optical size
alignment, color, semantic role, and labeling
screenshotLimits: the exact library and path cannot be identified with certainty
accessible names and RTL behavior are not visible

concepts.name: Content and layout resilience
concepts.description: Preserve readability, hierarchy, and actions when real content exceeds visible examples.
inspect: apparent width and height constraints
visible wrapping, clamping, ellipsis, and growth zones
dependencies between content and container size
screenshotLimits: short text does not prove an overflow strategy
fixed visible height does not prove resilience to zoom or translation

concepts.name: Semantic responsiveness and reflow
concepts.description: Define how priority, order, and function survive constrained space beyond simple breakpoints.
inspect: intrinsic containers and groups
essential versus secondary elements
evidence of wrap, local scroll, or reorganization
screenshotLimits: one viewport reveals no breakpoint
unshown hide, collapse, and reordering behavior remains proposed or unknown
stressTests: wide table in a narrow container

concepts.name: Localization and bidirectionality resilience
concepts.description: Anticipate string expansion, scripts, reading direction, and cultural formats without inventing an observed locale.
inspect: visible date, number, currency, and name formats
layout dependence on label length
culturally ambiguous colors or icons
screenshotLimits: one language does not prove internationalization
RTL, plurals, and alternate formats remain unobserved

concepts.name: Affordance and discoverability
concepts.description: Align appearance, available action, and understanding of the next step.
inspect: contrast and shape of interactive elements
labels, icons, and action cues
hierarchy of primary and secondary actions
screenshotLimits: interactive appearance does not prove the entire region responds
hover, focus, and shortcuts are not visible

concepts.name: Input-modality equivalence
concepts.description: Preserve the same useful outcome across keyboard, touch, pointer, and assistive technologies.
inspect: visible target size
probable order and grouping of controls
dependence on hover or an implicit gesture
screenshotLimits: real hit targets, DOM, and focus order are invisible
gestures and shortcuts cannot be certified

concepts.name: Spatial continuity and context preservation
concepts.description: Preserve orientation, focus, scroll, and mental context across transitions and returns.
inspect: navigation anchors and current location
spatial relation between trigger and result
embedded panels, dialogs, and details
screenshotLimits: focus return and scroll restoration are not visible
continuity across screens requires a sequence or a proposal

concepts.name: Progressive disclosure
concepts.description: Make complexity available when needed without imposing it at first glance.
inspect: primary and secondary information
menus, expandable details, and terminal actions
initial density and paths to depth
screenshotLimits: a closed panel does not reveal its content
placement alone does not establish usage frequency or product intent

concepts.name: Reversibility and forgiveness
concepts.description: Reduce the cost of mistakes through undo, rollback, proportionate confirmation, and work preservation.
inspect: visible destructive or consequential actions
confirmation, cancellation, or secondary action
precision of stated consequences
screenshotLimits: real undo and rollback availability is not proven
server-side effects remain unknown

concepts.name: Feedback proportionality and interruption budget
concepts.description: Choose inline, toast, banner, panel, or dialog feedback according to urgency, consequence, and expected action.
inspect: placement and intensity of visible statuses
relationship between message, cause, and action
use of color, icons, and attention levels
screenshotLimits: feedback duration and repetition remain invisible
a screenshot cannot prove screen-reader behavior

concepts.name: Data-scale resilience
concepts.description: Preserve comprehension and control with more rows, columns, series, statuses, or extreme values.
inspect: table or list density and anatomy
column and action priority
visible pagination, summaries, filters, and legends
screenshotLimits: real volume, virtualization, and backend limits are invisible
one data page does not prove extreme behavior
stressTests: zero, one, and ten thousand rows

concepts.name: Asset and media resilience
concepts.description: Define dimensions, cropping, loading, fallback, and purpose for images, logos, illustrations, and charts.
inspect: ratio, crop, density, and alignment
reserved space and content relationship
informative or decorative role
screenshotLimits: source files, licenses, alternate text, and fallbacks are invisible
a loaded asset does not reveal its loading state

concepts.name: Visual stability
concepts.description: Avoid shifts, flicker, and geometry changes that disrupt reading or action.
inspect: reserved spaces and stable dimensions
relationship between loaded state and container
visible sticky or overlaid elements
screenshotLimits: layout shift and flicker require a sequence or rendered test
runtime performance cannot be certified from pixels

concepts.name: Motion grammar
concepts.description: Propose functional, interruptible, reduced-motion-compatible motion without presenting static-screen deductions as observed.
inspect: spatial relationships that suggest origin or destination
state changes that benefit from continuity
hierarchy between immediate feedback and transition
screenshotLimits: duration, easing, and path are not observable in a screenshot
every absent rule must be proposed or unknown
stressTests: transition that must not alter layout

concepts.name: Accessibility semantics and annotations
concepts.description: Separate visible accessibility cues from DOM and behavioral requirements that implementation must verify.
inspect: visual order, grouping, and probable heading levels
visible labels, relative contrast, and non-color coding
compact targets and shown focus
screenshotLimits: conformance cannot be certified without DOM and tests
roles, accessible names, focus order, and live regions remain unknown

concepts.name: Trust, permission, and transparency
concepts.description: Explain provenance, freshness, access, and consequences when they affect a user decision.
inspect: provenance or freshness indicators
access badges, warnings, and permission labels
visible explanation of consequences
screenshotLimits: real policies, data processing, and permissions are invisible
an absent indicator does not prove an absent rule

concepts.name: Design-to-code and non-regression contract
concepts.description: Make extracted rules agent-usable, installable without duplication, and verifiable after generation.
inspect: tokens, relationships, and component contracts to export
required rules, recommendations, and anti-patterns
evidence, confidence, unknowns, and exceptions
screenshotLimits: a screenshot does not reveal the target framework or code structure
agent guidance does not mechanically enforce compliance
stressTests: audit of a newly generated page
